newsletters.title: The Gentlemen's Gazette — Season 4, No. 1 (Pre-Draft Edition)
newsletters.body:
State of the League

Where We Left Off

Three seasons in the books, three different champions, and 2025 gave us the wildest story yet. Here's the recap heading into Year Four.

🏆

Sam Trusty — 2025 League Champion

2-12 and dead last in 2024. 8-6 and hoisting the trophy twelve months later. The greatest single-season turnaround on record, capped by the league's best all-time bracket mark (4-1).

How the Playoffs Filled Out
2025 Playoff Bracket
Byes#1 Garrett Larson & #2 Kaden Smith
Round 1#5 Sam Trusty def. #4 Tyson Garff · #6 Rollin Rockett def. #3 Oliver Iverson
Semifinals#5 Sam Trusty def. #1 Garrett Larson · #2 Kaden Smith def. #6 Rollin Rockett
ChampionshipSam Trusty def. Kaden Smith
3rd PlaceGarrett Larson def. Rollin Rockett
5th PlaceTyson Garff def. Oliver Iverson

The 5-seed won it all. Sam Trusty needed three straight upsets — over the #1 seed in the semis, then Kaden Smith in the final — to complete the biggest turnaround in league history. Meanwhile, the top two seeds, Garrett Larson and Kaden Smith, both got byes and both still fell short of the trophy.

New This Year

Introducing Divisions

For the first time in league history, 2026 introduces divisions — three groups of four managers each. The assignments are randomized, not based on standings or power rankings, with one rule built in: every division is constructed around a rivalry pair, so you and your rival always land in the same group together.

Here's how that plays out across the schedule:

Weeks 1 & 14
Rivalry

You play your rival twice — once to open the season, once right before the playoffs begin.

Weeks 4, 6, 9, 11
Division

You play your other two division-mates, each twice across these four weeks.

Weeks 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13
Crossover

Everyone else in the league, each once.

Weeks 15–17
Playoffs

The six-team bracket, seeded off the regular season.

The rivalry is the whole point of the format. Whoever wins across both matchups — Week 1 and Week 14, combined — is the winner of the rivalry for the year and claims the trophy. Split the series 1-1 and total points across both games decide it.

The Big Picture

Year Four Is the Year to Create Separation

Three seasons is long enough to see real patterns — who's building something and who's still figuring it out. It's also long enough that the field is starting to sort itself into tiers, whether anyone's officially calling it that or not. 2026 is the season where the gap either closes or widens for good.

For the managers at the top, this is the year to stop trading titles back and forth and actually start stacking them — to be the manager everyone else is measured against instead of just the guy who won once. For everyone else, the clock is starting to matter: three years in, “still figuring it out” is getting harder to say with a straight face. Establish yourself now, or watch the gap become permanent.

Manager Watch

Every Situation, Every Storyline

Kaden Smith
Best Offense, No Ring

Kaden led the entire league in points scored in 2025 (1,822.88) and paced the field with 5 weekly high scores — more than any other manager. He still lost the championship, his second runner-up finish in three years. The trend line bounced back hard after a rough 9th-place year in 2024: 1st, 9th, 2nd. He's proven he can put up points; the ring keeps slipping away.

2026 OUTLOOKA second title cements him as the most dominant manager the league has ever seen. A third runner-up finish starts a very different conversation.
Jeffrey Taylor
The Slide Nobody's Talking About

Second-best career win percentage in the league, zero championships — and 2025 was his worst season yet. Dead last in points scored league-wide (1,452.8), a 5-9 finish, and a finish trend that's gone the wrong way three years running: 2nd, 4th, 7th. He's also been thoroughly owned by his rival Brandon Evans across their history (2-5).

The one bright spot: he closed the year with a win over Rollin Rockett, so there's at least something to build on.

2026 OUTLOOKEither this is the bottom of a real decline and 2026 turns it around, or the numbers are telling the real story now.
Chase Potter
From Champion to Cautionary Tale

The 2024 champion — a perfect 3-0 run through the bracket — fell all the way to 9th in 2025, his worst finish on record. But he ended the season on a 3-game win streak, capped by a win over Gavin Chowen in the finale. He also still leads his rivalry with Kaden Smith 2-1 in one of the league's tightest, highest-scoring series (148 PPG average).

2026 OUTLOOKThe late-season momentum makes him a sneaky buy-low team. One good draft and he's right back in the Tier I conversation.
Brandon Evans
The Streak That Finally Broke

Brandon built a reputation on steadiness — a .558 career win percentage and, until now, never a last-place finish. 2025 broke that: an 11th-place finish, his worst ever, and it came directly off a 3rd-place season. The one silver lining is a big one — he beat eventual champion Sam Trusty in the regular-season finale, and he continues to dominate his rivalry with Jeffrey Taylor (5-2).

2026 OUTLOOKWas 2025 the outlier, or is the 'steady' reputation no longer accurate? This is the year that answers it.
Tyson Garff
The Quiet Climb

Tied for the third-best career win percentage in the league, but still has never reached a championship game in three years. His finish trend is the most gradual, consistent improvement in the league — 7th, 6th, 5th — and he closed 2025 with a win over Britton Anderson. The one blemish: his rival, Sam Trusty, has dominated their series 4-1.

2026 OUTLOOKGood win percentage plus a rising trend line usually means a breakthrough is close. This looks like the year the climb turns into a real title run.
Garrett Larson
The League's Biggest Wildcard

Nobody swings harder than Garrett. A last-place, 3-11 finish in 2024 turned into the league's best record (10-4) and the #1 seed in 2025 — the sharpest one-year turnaround anyone's had. But as the top seed with a bye, he still lost in the semifinals to eventual champion Sam Trusty, and finished third despite having the best record in the league. He also holds a 3-1 edge over his rival Rollin Rockett.

2026 OUTLOOKThe variance says anything is possible — a genuine dynasty run or another crash back to the bottom. A #1 seed that loses in the semis is exactly the kind of result that can go either way next year.
Carston Christensen
Stuck in the Band

He literally named his 2025 team “2025 League Champion.” He finished 8th. That's on brand — in three seasons he's never finished better than 5th or worse than 9th, the narrowest range in the league. He does edge his rival Oliver Iverson 3-2 in a genuinely close series.

He's also 169 career moves deep — the most active roster in the entire league by a wide margin. Nobody manages their team harder week to week. If that activity ever lines up with the right waiver claims at the right time, it's exactly the kind of edge that catapults a mid-pack team into a real run.

2026 OUTLOOKHe's proven he won't collapse. All that roster management finally paying off in the standings is the breakout case for 2026.
Gavin Chowen
The Wildest Swing in the League

Even wilder than Garrett Larson's arc: a #1 seed and runner-up finish in 2024, then dead last in 2025. That's an 11th-to-2nd-to-12th trend — the single sharpest collapse anyone has had. He closed the year with a loss to Chase Potter, and his rivalry with Britton Anderson is basically a coin flip (he trails 2-3 in a series decided by less than a point per game on average).

2026 OUTLOOKHistory says a bounce is coming — nobody stays this far down after being this good the year before. But he has to prove the free-fall is over.
Oliver Iverson
The League's Most Improved, Still Unproven in the Bracket

Three straight years of real improvement — 9th, 8th, 6th — capped by his first playoff berth in 2025. He also finished with the third-most points scored in the league (1,663.12), ahead of every team except Kaden Smith and Garrett Larson. But as the 3-seed, he was bounced in the very first round by Rollin Rockett, and he closed the regular season with a shootout loss to Kaden Smith (146.84–155.94).

2026 OUTLOOKThe point totals already look like a contender. 2026 is about proving the offense can survive the first weekend of the playoffs.
Sam Trusty
Defending a Title Built on Timing, Not Points

The reigning champion had the lowest points-scored total of any of the six playoff teams in 2025 (1,595.3) — and still won it all, running a 4-1 bracket record, the best in league history. His finish trend (3rd, 11th, 1st) is a genuine rollercoaster, and he's dominated his rival Tyson Garff 4-1 across their history.

2026 OUTLOOKThis is the league's hardest team to predict. History says a low-scoring champion regresses. “Getting hot at the right time” is also a real, repeatable skill for some managers — the first title defense will tell us which kind of team this is.
Rollin Rockett
First Taste of the Playoffs — On a Bit of a Fluke

Rollin's climb has been the steadiest in the league (13th, 10th, 4th), capped by his first-ever playoff appearance and playoff win in 2025. But he backed into the postseason at 6-8 while losing three straight games to end the regular season, including a finale loss to Jeffrey Taylor. Once he got in, though, he actually won a bracket game before falling to Kaden Smith in the semis.

2026 OUTLOOKLast year's playoff run happened in spite of a late-season fade, not because of one. 2026 is about showing up with real form, not backing in again.
Britton Anderson
Still Waiting for Year One

The only manager in league history without a single playoff appearance across three seasons, and the trend isn't moving — 10th, 7th, 10th. He also posted the worst point differential in the entire league in 2025 (−11.4) despite a respectable 6-8 record, a sign of some genuinely ugly losses mixed in, and closed the year with a lopsided finale loss to Tyson Garff. He does hold a 3-2 edge over his rival Gavin Chowen — in a series that's essentially a coin flip.

2026 OUTLOOKThe numbers point to another tough year unless something structurally changes. But droughts like this tend to end exactly when nobody expects it.
What's At Stake

The 2026 Draft

Saturday, August 29th, in-person in Salt Lake City, Utah · 8:00 PM MT · $100 buy-in per manager.

1.Rollin Rockett
2.Oliver Iverson
3.Kaden Smith
4.Garrett Larson
5.Tyson Garff
6.Jeffrey Taylor
7.Carston Christensen
8.Brandon Evans
9.Chase Potter
10.Sam Trusty
11.Britton Anderson
12.Gavin Chowen
Location
Salt Lake City
Buy-In
$100

For Sam Trusty, it's a title defense with a hobbled franchise quarterback. For Kaden Smith, it's another shot at the ring that's eluded him twice. For Britton Anderson, it's a chance to finally end a three-year playoff drought. And with divisions and rivalries locked in for the first time, every manager has a built-in measuring stick from Week 1. Every pick means something.

Around the League

A Few More Things Worth Knowing

Rivalry to Watch

Kaden Smith and Chase Potter's series is the highest-scoring rivalry in the league by a wide margin — a combined 283.7 points per game on average, well clear of every other pair. Two Tier I offenses, a 2-1 edge for Chase, and no sign either side is slowing down.

The Gambling Desk

The league's got real money down on the Utah Jazz clearing 36.5 wins this year — six managers, $1,051.34 staked, $863.42 in potential profit on the table at -111. Call it the Jazz's own shot at completing “The Ascension” before this league's does.

By the Numbers — 2025 Leftovers

Highest PF average (2025)Kaden Smith (130.2/gm)
Worst point differential (2025)Britton Anderson (-11.4)
Most active roster (career moves)Carston Christensen (169)

Kaden's put up the league's best per-game average two years running — will it finally translate into a title? Britton's differential says he's losing the close ones badly against good offenses — can he catch a break there in 2026? And Carston's managed his roster harder than anyone in the league — the question is whether all that activity finally catapults him into real contention.

Coming Soon: The Locker Room

Every manager's trophy case, personal touches, and league lore, auto-updated from real results — currently under construction on the site. Look for it later this season.

newsletters.title: The Gentlemen's Gazette — Season 4, No. 2 (Draft Recap Edition)
newsletters.body:
Season Kickoff

Draft Night at The Lounge

Twelve managers, sixteen rounds, and a whole lot of trash talk — Season 4's draft went down live at The Lounge on Sunday, August 30th, and it delivered exactly the kind of night you want to kick off a fantasy season. Good food, better company, and just enough tension in the room every time a run started on a position to make you second-guess your board. Whoever's idea it was to do this one in person again, thank you — there's no substitute for watching someone's face in real time when their guy gets sniped one pick early.

Draft Recap

Grading All Twelve Draft Rooms

Since nobody's played a game yet, these grades aren't the site's usual points-above-replacement math — that needs a real season to work. This is a straight film-and-market read: current 2026 ADP, real depth charts, real injury reports as of this week, and what each roster actually looks like when you put the whole thing together.

Carston Christensen (Ascension) A+
Best Draft in the League

Jaxon Smith-Njigba — the reigning real-life Offensive Player of the Year after leading the NFL in receiving yards — at #7 overall is a legitimate top-five overall talent falling to the middle of round one. Then Trey McBride at the 2/6 turn, a tight end some rankings have as high as TE1 overall, is absurd value that late. Add Malik Nabers in round three and this roster has three genuine WR1s. Jalen Hurts is coming off a down year by his own standard, which is the one real question mark, but the weapons around him at receiver are unmatched anywhere in this draft.

2026 OUTLOOKThis is the best collection of pass-catching talent in the league, full stop. Currently #7 in the Power Rankings feels light given what's actually on this roster.
Oliver Iverson (Auto) A
RB1 Certainty, WR Depth for Days

Jahmyr Gibbs at #2 overall is about as safe a foundation as this format allows — he just landed a three-year, $67.5M extension that edged out both Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor, and he's coming off a season with 49 total touchdowns since entering the league. Grabbing Jeremiyah Love at the 2/11 turn was tremendous value; the Cardinals' No. 3 overall pick is drawing real "my guy" buzz from national analysts as a top-10 rookie back. Add Nico Collins, Jaylen Waddle, and Tee Higgins for a WR room three teams deep, plus Kyle Pitts at TE. The one soft spot is quarterback — Caleb Williams is a name, not a proven weekly starter yet.

2026 OUTLOOKIf Gibbs and Love both stay healthy, this is a top-two offense in the league on paper. Auto is currently #1 in the Power Rankings, and the roster backs it up.
Kaden Smith (JadenSmith99) A
Elite WR1, Elite TE Value, Deep Backfield

Ja'Marr Chase at #3 overall remains one of the two or three best fantasy assets in the sport when Joe Burrow is healthy. Landing Brock Bowers at the 2/10 turn is exceptional value — some 2026 boards have him as the outright TE1. Bucky Irving, Javonte Williams, and a deep committee behind them give real running back insurance, and DJ Moore adds a proven second option outside. Dak Prescott is a sneaky-solid streaming option at QB with real weapons around him in real life. The Power Rankings have this roster at #10, which looks like the single biggest gap between reputation and roster in the league.

2026 OUTLOOKOn paper, this might be a top-three roster. If the results catch up to the talent, this is the team everyone else should be worried about.
Tyson Garff (Team Garff) A-
Christian McCaffrey's Health Is the Whole Season

Landing Josh Allen — the unanimous #1 fantasy quarterback for a sixth straight year — at the 3/5 turn is one of the single best value picks anywhere in this draft. The concern is round one: McCaffrey is entering his age-30 season, and San Francisco has been visibly cautious with his workload in camp after his lost 2024. When he's on the field he's still a top-three back in the league; the question is how many weeks that actually is. A.J. Brown's fresh start in New England and DK Metcalf's move to Pittsburgh give this roster two change-of-scenery bets with real upside, and Terry McLaurin adds a proven third option.

2026 OUTLOOKJosh Allen alone makes this a playoff-caliber roster. A full season of McCaffrey turns it into the team to beat.
Brandon Evans (Shire King) A-
The Best Running Back Room in the League

Jonathan Taylor at #8 overall just signed a $22M-per-year extension as one of the league's featured backs, and pairing him with Derrick Henry at the 2/5 turn gives this roster a 1-2 RB punch nobody else in the draft can match — even with Henry entering his age-32 season. Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, and Rome Odunze round out a genuinely deep WR corps, and Patrick Mahomes at QB in the back half of the draft is pure luxury — a top-five real-life passer taken as a QB2. Mark Andrews gives a credible TE1 if he stays on the field.

2026 OUTLOOKTaylor and Henry alone could be worth 30+ points most weeks between them. This is a contender's roster if the receiving corps produces one true alpha.
Gavin Chowen (Team Chowen) B+
Boom-or-Bust at the Top, Steals in the Middle

De'Von Achane at #12 overall is the swing pick of this whole draft — electric talent, but Miami lost run-game-friendly play-caller Mike McDaniel and the offense around him is a real question. If the volume holds, he's a top-five back; if the offense stalls, this pick ages fast. The saving grace is everything after it: Chase Brown gives a genuine RB2 floor, Colston Loveland was one of the best rookie tight ends in the league down the stretch last year and comes in as a consensus top-three TE for 2026, and Joe Burrow in round six is a massive value if his line and weapons hold up. Travis Hunter in round eleven is one of the more fascinating picks in the draft — two-way superstar, unclear exact usage.

2026 OUTLOOKHigh variance, high ceiling. This roster's floor is 'solid,' but the outcomes range all the way up to 'best team in the league' if Achane's workload holds.
Jeffrey Taylor (DarrynWaynePeterson) B+
Elite Floor at WR, Banking on a Committee

Amon-Ra St. Brown at #6 is a rock-solid WR1 anchor, and George Pickens landing in Dallas next to CeeDee Lamb in real life is one of the best value swings in this draft — a true #2 receiver getting #1 targets on a lot of weeks. Kenneth Walker III's move to Kansas City adds a change of scenery that could unlock more work, and the running back room (Walker, Rico Dowdle, Rhamondre Stevenson, Isiah Pacheco) is deep enough to survive an injury. Tyler Warren at tight end is a real name in the rookie hype conversation, but he's still unproven — and there's no true bell-cow lead back on this roster, just good pieces.

2026 OUTLOOKWeekly floor is high across the board. The ceiling depends on one of those committee backs pulling away from the pack.
Rollin Rockett (NFL YoungBoy) B
Bijan Anchors It, the QB Room Needs a Streamer

Bijan Robinson at #1 overall — fresh off a three-year, $75M extension that made him the highest-paid running back in NFL history — is as good a foundation as exists in this format. Chris Olave, Rashee Rice, and Davante Adams give real receiver volume, and George Kittle remains one of the most reliable weekly tight ends in the league. The soft spot is obvious: Trevor Lawrence, Jared Goff, and Tyler Shough is a QB room built on hope rather than plan. In a league this deep at quarterback, that's a real problem to solve on the waiver wire early.

2026 OUTLOOKBijan alone keeps this competitive every week. Whoever ends up starting at QB by midseason will decide how far this team actually goes.
Sam Trusty (Sammoth.ai) B
Betting Big on Justin Jefferson's Bounce-Back

Justin Jefferson at #10 overall is the classic buy-low superstar — a genuinely elite receiver who had his numbers wrecked last year by a rookie quarterback's rough season, not by anything wrong with Jefferson himself. If the Vikings' passing game is even league-average this year, he's a top-five WR again. Drake Maye at the 5/10 turn, after breaking out into a legitimate QB2 in real-life scoring last season, is outstanding value. Omarion Hampton adds a promising young back, though Marvin Harrison Jr.'s continued inconsistency as a sophomore is a real question mark in the middle rounds.

2026 OUTLOOKThe whole season hinges on one bet: does Jefferson's quarterback situation actually improve? If yes, this roster jumps tiers.
Britton Anderson (Dojah) B-
Strong Backfield, High-Variance QB Bet

James Cook III and Saquon Barkley give this roster two legitimate every-week backs, even with Barkley entering the back half of his prime. DeVonta Smith and Emeka Egbuka provide a steady, if not explosive, receiving floor. The real swing is Jayden Daniels — a genuine MVP-caliber talent when healthy, but he lost most of last season to injury, and everything about this roster's ceiling depends on him staying on the field with a full complement of weapons. Harold Fannin Jr. is a sneaky late-round tight end flier with real rookie buzz.

2026 OUTLOOKSafe floor, uncertain ceiling. A healthy Daniels turns this into a sneaky-good roster; another injury-shortened year caps it hard.
Chase Potter (Turbo) C+
Highest Ceiling in the League, Real Injury Risk

CeeDee Lamb at #9 is a proven WR1, but the round-two swing on Ashton Jeanty is the story of this whole roster: the new coaching staff in Las Vegas wants to use him like prime Christian McCaffrey, which is a massive-usage dream scenario — except he's currently dealing with an ankle injury that's creating real uncertainty heading into Week 1. Lamar Jackson in round four is boom-or-bust after an injury-marred, rushing-diminished 2025, but a two-time MVP with a new play-caller has real bounce-back equity. If both hits land, this is a scary roster. If they don't, it's a long year.

2026 OUTLOOKThe widest range of outcomes in the league. Monitor Jeanty's ankle closely — it may decide the first month of this team's season.
Garrett Larson (Team Larson) C
Elite WR1, Murky Everywhere Else

Puka Nacua at #4 overall is about as safe a first-round anchor as exists — a career 95.3 yards-per-game average that's the best mark in NFL history, and he's already back at full practice after a minor camp injury. Drake London gives a strong second option. After that, this roster gets muddier: Breece Hall, Bhayshul Tuten, and Rachaad White form a running back committee without a clear lead, and Sam LaPorta's tight end role has come with real target-share questions the last two years, with Travis Kelce as an aging backup plan. Justin Herbert at 4/9 is legitimate value at quarterback, at least.

2026 OUTLOOKNacua carries this team on his own if he stays on the field. Everyone else needs to sort itself out for this roster to compete.
The Big Picture

Early Championship Radar

Three teams worth watching before a single snap has been played, based on what actually landed on each roster.

Carston Christensen (Ascension)

The favorite. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Trey McBride, and Malik Nabers is a three-deep collection of pass-catching talent nobody else in the league can match — JSN is the reigning real-life Offensive Player of the Year, McBride grades as a top-two tight end, and Nabers is one of the best young receivers in football. Jalen Hurts coming off a down year is the only real question. If forced to pick one team to win it all today, this is it.

Brandon Evans (Shire King)

Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry give this roster the best 1-2 running back punch in the league, full stop — Taylor just signed a $22M/year extension as a featured back, and Henry is still producing at an elite level even in his 30s. Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, and Rome Odunze add real depth at receiver, and Patrick Mahomes as a QB2 luxury pick rounds out one of the most complete rosters in the draft.

Tyson Garff (Team Garff)

Getting Josh Allen — the unanimous #1 fantasy quarterback for six straight years — at the 3/5 turn is a massive market inefficiency, and it alone makes this a playoff-caliber roster regardless of what happens elsewhere. The swing factor is Christian McCaffrey's health; San Francisco has been cautious with his workload in camp entering his age-30 season. A full season of a healthy CMC on top of the Allen value makes this the team to beat.

Week 1

Rivalry Week Predictions

Every manager opens the season against their designated rival — the same six pairs that will run it back in Week 14 right before the playoffs. Here's how the film says it breaks, matchup by matchup, topped by the game of the week.

★ Matchup of the Week
Kaden Smith
@
Chase Potter 🏆
PICK: Chase Potter

This is the marquee game of the week, and it's not about the Power Rankings — JadenSmith99 sits at #10 and Turbo at #9, two of the lower-ranked teams in the league on paper. It's about who these two managers are. Kaden Smith owns the #1 all-time Power Score in league history and the best career win percentage (.628) anyone's ever posted — and he's still chasing his second ring. Chase Potter's 2024 title run was a perfect 3-0 sweep through the bracket as a #3 seed, one of the cleanest championship runs on record. All-time, Chase actually leads the series 2-1, averaging 148.0 points per game to Kaden's 135.7 — one of the highest-scoring rivalries in the league. Their most recent meeting was a shootout: Kaden won 160.2–124.1 in 2025 Week 7, cutting the gap to just one game. On rosters, Kaden's draft graded out as one of the best in the league (Ja'Marr Chase at #3 overall, Brock Bowers at outstanding value), a real mismatch with his #10 ranking. Chase Potter's draft has the single highest ceiling in the building — CeeDee Lamb at #9, and a round-two swing on Ashton Jeanty that could pay off enormously under a new coaching staff that wants to use him like prime Christian McCaffrey. The catch: Jeanty is dealing with an ankle injury right now, which puts a real asterisk on Turbo's ceiling this specific week. A Kaden win evens the rivalry at 2-2 and pressures the Power Rankings to catch up to his roster; a Chase win, especially with a hobbled Jeanty, would be the more impressive version of pushing the series to 3-1. Expect fireworks either way — this series doesn't do low-scoring.

Oliver Iverson
@
Carston Christensen 🏆
PICK: Carston Christensen

Two of the best-drafted rosters in the entire league happen to be rivals, and they're playing each other in Week 1. Oliver's Jahmyr Gibbs plus Jeremiyah Love gives him a legitimate two-back attack, but Carston's receiving corps — Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Trey McBride, Malik Nabers — is the best collection of pass-catching talent anywhere in the league, real-life OPOY included. The all-time series has been close (Carston leads 3-2), and with Jalen Hurts capable of spreading the ball to three legitimate WR1s, this should be a shootout. Slight edge to Ascension.

Gavin Chowen
@
Britton Anderson 🏆
PICK: Britton Anderson

Britton's James Cook III/Saquon Barkley combo gives Dojah a steadier week-to-week floor than Gavin's Achane-centric build, which still carries real uncertainty now that Miami has lost its run-game-friendly play-caller. Britton also holds the rivalry lead at 3-2 all-time. That said, Gavin's roster has the higher ceiling if De'Von Achane's workload holds — Chase Brown and a red-hot Colston Loveland give him real firepower beyond the headline running back. Lean Dojah on the safer bet, but a big Achane week flips this fast.

Tyson Garff 🏆
@
Sam Trusty
PICK: Tyson Garff

Sam owns this rivalry historically (4-1) and has a genuine bounce-back bet in Justin Jefferson — if the Vikings' passing game is even league-average, Jefferson is a top-five receiver again. But Tyson's roster is simply loaded from top to bottom: Josh Allen is the best real quarterback in the sport by a wide margin, and a healthy Christian McCaffrey outproduces almost anyone at his position. Drake Maye's breakout has been great value for Sam, but talent wins this one over history and bounce-back hope.

Rollin Rockett 🏆
@
Garrett Larson
PICK: Rollin Rockett

Garrett has won this rivalry three times to Rollin's one, and Puka Nacua — one of the safest first-round anchors in the league — gives Team Larson a real weekly floor. But Bijan Robinson, fresh off becoming the highest-paid running back in NFL history, is a full tier above anything on Garrett's roster, and Rollin's receiver depth (Chris Olave, Rashee Rice, Davante Adams) should hold up comfortably against Team Larson's muddled running back committee of Breece Hall, Bhayshul Tuten, and Rachaad White. Rollin snaps the skid here.

Jeffrey Taylor
@
Brandon Evans 🏆
PICK: Brandon Evans

The best combined Power Ranking matchup of the week (#2 vs. #3), and the history is lopsided — Brandon leads the all-time series 5-2. Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry give Shire King the single best running back duo in the league by a wide margin, and that's a tough matchup for anyone. Jeffrey's roster is deep — Amon-Ra St. Brown and a great value pickup in George Pickens give him real weapons — but there's no true lead back the way Brandon has two, and that gap is enough to keep the streak alive for Shire King.

newsletters.title: The Gentlemen's Gazette — Season 4, No. 3 (Week 1 Recap)
newsletters.body:
Week 1 in the Books

Rivalry Week Delivers

Six games, six rivalries, and the film matched the results: every single Week 1 pick in the last newsletter hit. 6-0. Let's not get used to that. Below: the full Week 1 recap, an update on the marquee matchup, and predictions for a Week 2 slate that already has real injury news to account for.

Week 1 Recap

Rivalry Week Results

Oliver Iverson 108.86
final
Carston Christensen 140.92

Ascension looked every bit the best-drafted roster in the league: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.2) and Trey McBride (24.5) both delivered, and Jalen Hurts had his best game of the young season (24.72). Oliver's Caleb Williams actually went off for 37.26, but Jaylen Waddle (1.2) and Kyle Pitts (0.0) no-showed and sank the rest of the lineup.

Gavin Chowen 71.66
final
Britton Anderson 75.66

The lowest-scoring game of the week, and it turned out to be a genuine piece of league history: at a combined 147.32 points, it's now the 5th-lowest-scoring game ever played in this league, bumping a 2025 Week 14 game out of the all-time bottom five. De'Von Achane's offense-context concerns showed up immediately — just 10.6 points in a quiet Miami outing. Britton's floor-over-ceiling build (James Cook III, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith) was exactly steady enough to escape with the win.

Kaden Smith 111.5
final
Chase Potter 134.66

The Matchup of the Week lived up to the billing — full recap below.

Rollin Rockett 146.6
final
Garrett Larson 97.06

Bijan Robinson (31.3), David Montgomery (28.9), and Chris Olave (28.2) all popped in the same week for Rollin, who put up the week's second-highest score and snapped his 1-3 skid in this rivalry with room to spare. Garrett's Puka Nacua stayed quiet (12.4), and the running back committee (Breece Hall, Bhayshul Tuten) didn't produce enough to keep pace.

Jeffrey Taylor 145.7
final
Brandon Evans 153.94

The single biggest storyline of the week, and it wasn't even the final score. Jeffrey put up the week's second-highest total (145.7) and still lost — because he left 118.4 points on the bench, a new all-time league record for points left unused in a single week, breaking Sam Trusty's old mark of 110.22 (2025, Week 4) by more than 8 points. Christian Watson alone scored 32.7 points on Jeffrey's bench, and Jalen Coker added another 33.8 — between those two players alone, Jeffrey benched more points than most managers score in a full week. Brandon's Jonathan Taylor (25.1) and Derrick Henry (35.3) combined for 60.4 points to post the week's single highest score and extend his series lead to 5-2.

Tyson Garff 124.66
final
Sam Trusty 105.52

Josh Allen (35.66) and D'Andre Swift (34.2) carried Tyson to the win, snapping Sam's 4-1 hold on this rivalry. Justin Jefferson looked fully bounced-back with 31.2 points for Sam, but it wasn't enough on its own.

★ Matchup of the Week Recap
🏈

Chase Potter Takes Round 4

Chase Potter beat Kaden Smith 134.66–111.5, pushing the all-time series to 3-1 and validating the single boldest bet of the whole draft: Ashton Jeanty. Coming in with real Week 1 uncertainty around his ankle, Jeanty went out and posted 32.7 points on 29 touches, 147 total yards, and two touchdowns against Miami — exactly the workload his new coaching staff promised. CeeDee Lamb (15.4) and Lamar Jackson (24.96) rounded out a complete team win.

Kaden's roster wasn't the problem — Ja'Marr Chase (20.3) and DJ Moore (21.0) both delivered — but Dak Prescott's modest 14.4 and a quiet Bucky Irving (13.5) left him short. The series now sits at 3-1 Chase, and the average score in this rivalry (123.1 combined this week) continues to run well above the league norm. Kaden still owns the better all-time resume, but he needs a signature win in this series to start closing the gap.

Week 2

Crossover Week Predictions

Every team plays outside its division this week. A few real injury developments from around the league factor directly into these picks — most notably a timeshare backfield in San Francisco and an IR designation that hits one roster hard.

★ Matchup of the Week
Britton Anderson
@
Carston Christensen 🏆
PICK: Carston Christensen

It pits Dojah's steady floor against the most talented roster in the league on paper. Ascension's receiving corps (Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Trey McBride, Malik Nabers) was electric in Week 1, and there's no reason to expect a letdown here. Britton's James Cook III/Saquon Barkley combo keeps this competitive, but Ascension should stay perfect.

Chase Potter 🏆
@
Tyson Garff
PICK: Chase Potter

Real news changes this pick: Christian McCaffrey is now sharing San Francisco's backfield with rookie Kaelon Black, who actually out-touched him in Week 1 (14 carries to CMC's 10). Worse for Tyson, A.J. Brown is now on IR with a high-ankle sprain. Meanwhile Chase Potter's Ashton Jeanty just looked like a top-five back in the league. Lean Turbo in a game that looked like a Team Garff lock a week ago.

Kaden Smith
@
Oliver Iverson 🏆
PICK: Oliver Iverson

Both teams are 0-1 despite being two of the best-drafted rosters in the league — something has to give. Oliver's receiver depth (Nico Collins, Jaylen Waddle, Tee Higgins) gives him more paths to a big score than Kaden's more top-heavy build, and the home matchup nudges this to Auto to get back on track.

Gavin Chowen
@
Rollin Rockett 🏆
PICK: Rollin Rockett

Rollin is coming off the week's second-highest score, with Bijan Robinson, David Montgomery, and Chris Olave all clicking at once. Gavin's De'Von Achane concern showed up immediately in Week 1 (10.6 points), and until Miami's offense proves it can support him, this is a tough spot for Team Chowen on the road.

Sam Trusty
@
Jeffrey Taylor 🏆
PICK: Jeffrey Taylor

Jeffrey scored the week's second-most points and still lost — the roster clearly isn't the problem, the lineup card was. If he simply starts his best players (Christian Watson chief among them), this is a dangerous team at home. Sam's Justin Jefferson bounce-back is real, but one player alone doesn't offset a full-roster lineup correction on the other side.

Brandon Evans 🏆
@
Garrett Larson
PICK: Brandon Evans

Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry combined for the week's highest score, and that floor alone should be enough here even with Zay Flowers dealing with a re-aggravated hamstring that's worth monitoring. Garrett's running back committee (Breece Hall, Bhayshul Tuten, Rachaad White) still hasn't sorted itself out, and Puka Nacua being quiet in Week 1 is a concern if it continues.

By the Numbers

Records Set in Week 1

Most points left on the bench, single week (all-time): Jeffrey Taylor, 118.4 points, Week 1 2026. Breaks the previous record of 110.22, set by Sam Trusty in 2025 Week 4. Christian Watson (32.7) and Jalen Coker (33.8) alone outscored what most managers' entire benches produce in a week.

Lowest-scoring game, all-time (top 5): Team Chowen 71.66 – Dojah 75.66 (Week 1 2026), combined 147.32 points. The 5th-lowest-scoring game in league history, bumping a 2025 Week 14 game out of the all-time bottom five.

Implications

What Week 1 Actually Changed

Oliver Iverson's Auto came in as the #1 team in the Power Rankings and lost outright — a reminder that draft-day grades are not a guarantee, especially when two of your top weapons no-show in the same week. Kaden Smith's JadenSmith99, meanwhile, remains the league's clearest gap between roster talent and results: a strong loss to a 3-1 rival doesn't change that Ja'Marr Chase and Brock Bowers are still elite building blocks.

The bigger story is Jeffrey Taylor. Scoring the week's second-highest total and still losing, on the back of an all-time record for points benched, is either the unluckiest possible Week 1 or a five-alarm fire about his lineup-setting process. Either way, if he fixes it, DarrynWaynePeterson is a real threat — the roster is clearly good enough.

And keep an eye on San Francisco: if Christian McCaffrey is really in a committee with Kaelon Black, that reshapes Team Garff's outlook more than anything that happened on the field in Week 1. Josh Allen's value doesn't change. CMC's workload might.

Week 2 in the Books

Chalk Holds, Then the Trade Machine Gets Busy

Week 2 mostly went the way the rosters said it should — the four teams still unbeaten are exactly the four you'd expect from the preseason grades. But the real story of the week happened after the games: two separate blockbuster trades reshaped four rosters heading into Week 3. Full recap, both trades, the records that fell, and a fresh set of Week 3 predictions below.

SEASON PREDICTION RECORD: 10-2 (83%)
Week 2 Recap

Crossover Week Results

Chase Potter 98.3
final
Tyson Garff 115.12
❌ Predicted: Chase Potter

Josh Allen went off for 40.82 — his best game of the young season — and Christian McCaffrey chipped in 22.6 to push Tyson to 2-0. CeeDee Lamb (35.3) kept Chase competitive on his own, but the rest of the Lamb Chops lineup couldn't match Team Garff's floor.

Kaden Smith 124.16
final
Oliver Iverson 92.92
❌ Predicted: Oliver Iverson

Dak Prescott (29.76) and Ja'Marr Chase (26.5) led the way as Kaden bounced back from the Matchup of the Week loss to even his record at 1-1. Oliver's Jahmyr Gibbs (23.3) had a strong day, but too many zeros elsewhere — Nico Collins and DJ Moore combined for basically nothing.

Britton Anderson 107.84
final
Carston Christensen 124.06
✅ Predicted: Carston Christensen

The Matchup of the Week lived up to the hype — full recap below.

Gavin Chowen 96.08
final
Rollin Rockett 126.36
✅ Predicted: Rollin Rockett

Davante Adams exploded for 39.5 points to headline Rollin's second straight win. Gavin's De'Von Achane concerns are becoming a pattern — a modest 12.3 points in Week 2 after a quiet Week 1 — and Team Chowen drops to 0-2.

Sam Trusty 94.52
final
Jeffrey Taylor 149.48
✅ Predicted: Jeffrey Taylor

Amon-Ra St. Brown (35.2) and Brock Purdy (28.48) powered Jeffrey to the week's highest score and a 54.96-point win — now the third-worst blowout loss of Sam Trusty's four-season career, trailing only an 84.92-point loss in 2024 and a 60.16-point loss also in 2024. Justin Jefferson's bounce-back bet is stuck at a disappointing 8.5 points, and Sammoth.ai falls to 0-2.

Brandon Evans 133.48
final
Garrett Larson 129.68
✅ Predicted: Brandon Evans

The closest game of the week. Jonathan Taylor (29.2) and Patrick Mahomes (28.98) got Brandon to 2-0, but Garrett's Travis Kelce (25.1) and a big night from the Patriots D/ST (20.0) made it a real fight down to the final stat correction — a 3.8-point margin that's now the third-closest game of Garrett's career.

★ Matchup of the Week Recap
🏈

Ascension Stays Perfect

Carston Christensen beat Britton Anderson 124.06–107.84 in the only game of the week between two undefeated teams, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba made sure it wasn't close for long — 42.5 points, by far the best individual performance of the week and a real argument for the league's best receiver right now. Trey McBride (18.1) and Parker Washington (16.8) rounded out a complete team win.

Britton's DeVonta Smith had a monster day of his own (27.7), and James Cook III chipped in 20.9, but Malik Nabers going for just 1.1 points on Carston's side barely mattered — that's how deep this Ascension roster is. Carston moves to 2-0 and looks every bit like the best team in the league right now, exactly as the draft grades suggested back in Week 1.

Trade Desk

Two Blockbusters This Week

TRADE 1

Lamb Chops (Chase Potter) sends Jadarian Price and Carnell Tate to DarrynWaynePeterson (Jeffrey Taylor) for Jalen Coker and Chris Rodriguez Jr.

A depth-for-depth swap that barely moves the needle for either side — none of the four players were starting significant snaps in either lineup this week. More notable for timing than substance: it closed the same week Jeffrey posted the league's highest score, so consider it a quiet vote of confidence in a roster that's finally clicking.

TRADE 2

Cooper Kupping my balls (Rollin Rockett) sends Rashee Rice, Davante Adams, and David Montgomery to Team Larson (Garrett Larson) for Breece Hall, Jameson Williams, and Puka Nacua.

The real blockbuster of the week — a three-for-three headlined by Puka Nacua changing hands. On paper this looks like a clear win for Rollin: Nacua is a top-five receiver when healthy, and he's now 2-0 with real WR1 upside added to a roster that already has Bijan Robinson. But the timing is awkward — reports out this week have Nacua dealing with an injury that could keep him out for his very first game in a Cooper Kupping my balls uniform. Garrett, meanwhile, gets Rashee Rice at the exact moment national analysts are questioning his role in Kansas City's offense with Travis Kelce more involved than expected. Neither immediate return looks great; this is a trade that'll take a few weeks to properly grade.

Division Power Rankings

How the Three Divisions Stack Up in 2026

Based on this season only (two weeks in): combined record, and points scored per game.

#1 DIVISION III

Jeffrey Taylor, Brandon Evans, Carston Christensen, Oliver Iverson

5-3 combined (62.5%) · 131.2 points per game

#2 DIVISION II

Tyson Garff, Garrett Larson, Sam Trusty, Rollin Rockett

4-4 combined (50.0%) · 117.4 points per game

#3 DIVISION I

Kaden Smith, Chase Potter, Gavin Chowen, Britton Anderson

3-5 combined (37.5%) · 102.5 points per game

Small sample, but Division III is off to the best start in the league — Carston Christensen and Brandon Evans are both 2-0, and even Jeffrey Taylor's lone win came with the week's highest score. Division I, by contrast, is the only division with a sub-.500 combined record two weeks in, dragged down by Auto and Team Chowen both sitting at 0-2.

By the Numbers

Records and Notes From Week 2

Biggest personal blowout, Sam Trusty: the 54.96-point loss to Jeffrey Taylor is now the third-worst beating of Sam's four-season career, trailing only a 84.92-point loss in 2024 and a 60.16-point loss also in 2024. Rough stretch continues at 0-2.

Closest game, Garrett Larson: the 3.8-point loss to Brandon Evans is now the third-closest game of Garrett's career — and his second sub-4-point finish in the last calendar year.

Best individual performance of the week: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 42.5 points. Not a full-league record, but comfortably the best single performance either team has produced through two weeks of 2026.

Standings shake-up: four teams sit at 2-0 (Ascension, Cooper Kupping my balls, Team Garff, Shire King), and interestingly it's a clean split from the preseason Power Rankings — Auto, ranked #1 entering the season, is now 0-2 alongside Team Chowen and Sammoth.ai.

Week 3

Crossover Week Predictions

Both trades are live for Week 3, and real injury news around Puka Nacua and Rashee Rice's underwhelming role factor directly into a few of these calls.

★ Matchup of the Week
Garrett Larson
@
Jeffrey Taylor 🏆
PICK: Jeffrey Taylor

Both rosters were just reshaped by trades this week, and both managers are trying to answer the same question in real time: did the deal actually help? Garrett's new WR1, Rashee Rice, is currently being questioned by national analysts as Kansas City leans on Travis Kelce more than expected. Jeffrey, fresh off the week's highest score, has the safer floor with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Kenneth Walker III. Lean Jeffrey to keep rolling.

Oliver Iverson
@
Chase Potter 🏆
PICK: Chase Potter

Oliver is 0-2 despite a legitimately strong roster on paper, and something has to give soon. CeeDee Lamb just posted 35.3 points for Chase, and Ashton Jeanty is overdue for another big workload game. Lean Turbo at home.

Kaden Smith
@
Rollin Rockett 🏆
PICK: Rollin Rockett

Rollin is 2-0 and just added Puka Nacua to a roster that already had Bijan Robinson and Davante Adams... except reports this week suggest Nacua could be out for his Cooper Kupping my balls debut. Even accounting for that, Bijan Robinson and a red-hot Davante Adams should be enough against Kaden's still-finding-its-footing lineup.

Brandon Evans 🏆
@
Britton Anderson
PICK: Brandon Evans

Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry remain the best running back duo in the league, and Brandon is 2-0 with the week's second-highest score already banked. Britton's DeVonta Smith is playing like a legitimate WR1, but the running back floor on the other side should be the deciding factor.

Gavin Chowen
@
Tyson Garff 🏆
PICK: Tyson Garff

Josh Allen just posted a 40-point week, and Tyson is 2-0 with the best quarterback value in the entire draft still paying off. Gavin's De'Von Achane situation continues to look shaky through two weeks, and Team Chowen needs a full-roster bounce-back, not just one big Achane game, to get back in this one.

Carston Christensen 🏆
@
Sam Trusty
PICK: Carston Christensen

Ascension is the best team in the league right now and coming off a 42.5-point Jaxon Smith-Njigba masterclass. Sam is 0-2 and reeling from the worst blowout loss of his career last week. This isn't close on paper.

Implications

What Week 2 Actually Changed

The four teams at 2-0 — Ascension, Cooper Kupping my balls, Team Garff, and Shire King — are starting to separate from the pack, and none of it is a surprise given the preseason grades. What's more interesting is Auto sitting at 0-2 despite entering the season as the #1 team in the Power Rankings; two straight weeks of a quiet Nico Collins and DJ Moore have undone what looked like the deepest receiver room in the league on paper.

The two trades add a real subplot to watch. If Puka Nacua is actually out for Week 3, Rollin's blockbuster looks lopsided out of the gate no matter how good it is long-term — and if Rashee Rice keeps getting out-targeted by his own tight end, Garrett's side of the deal gets harder to defend. Neither team needed to make a move sitting at the records they're at (2-0 and 0-2 respectively), which says something about how much both managers believe in the long game over the early results.

newsletters.body:
Week 3 in the Books

Four Teams Still Standing

Three weeks in, and the league has split cleanly into three tiers: four teams still unbeaten, one team on a real heater, and three teams staring up at 0-3. Full recap, the record that fell (again), and a loaded Week 4 slate below — headlined by the last two undefeated teams left in the league meeting head-to-head.

SEASON PREDICTION RECORD: 15-3 (83%)
Week 3 Recap

Crossover Week Results

Carston Christensen 126.88
final
Sam Trusty 55.16

The Matchup of the Week — full recap below.

Oliver Iverson 121.12
final
Lamb Chops 104.84

Jahmyr Gibbs put together the best individual performance of the week (41.4) — he's now on pace for one of the best running back seasons in league history through three games. Oliver snaps a two-game skid to move to 1-2. Chase's CeeDee Lamb (20.2) and Kyren Williams (21.8) both showed up, but it wasn't enough to overcome a quiet night from Ashton Jeanty.

Kaden Smith 129.44
final
Rollin Rockett 141.36

Bijan Robinson (35.3) kept Rollin perfect at 3-0, and Puka Nacua's much-discussed Cooper Kupping my balls debut never happened — he was a healthy scratch, exactly the risk flagged when the trade went down. Kaden's Brock Bowers made his own season debut and delivered immediately (27.6), and Ja'Marr Chase added 24.8, but it wasn't quite enough on the road.

Brandon Evans 127.14
final
Britton Anderson 122.98

The closest game of the week. Derrick Henry (21.9) and a huge night from Jaylen Warren (20.6) got Brandon to 3-0, but Britton's Michael Wilson (25.9) and Harold Fannin Jr. (24.1 off the bench) made it a real fight to the final stat correction.

Gavin Chowen 80.44
final
Team Garff 136.86

Drake London (28.4) and a strong all-around effort got Tyson to 3-0 and handed Gavin his third straight loss. De'Von Achane's rough season continued — just 1.7 points — while Joe Burrow (22.58) went off from the bench, another lineup decision that's starting to define Team Chowen's season.

Garrett Larson 117.4
final
Jeffrey Taylor 146.98

Brock Purdy (31.28) headlined a complete team effort as Jeffrey won his second straight to move to 2-1. Garrett's new-look receiving corps (Rashee Rice, Davante Adams) both delivered 20+ points, but it wasn't enough to keep pace — Team Larson falls to 0-3.

★ Matchup of the Week Recap
🏈

Ascension Isn't Just Good — It's Historic

Carston Christensen demolished Sam Trusty 126.88–55.16, and the story wasn't the final score — it was Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 35.36 points, giving him 104.06 through three games, the fourth-most any player has ever scored through a season's first three weeks. Ascension is now 3-0 and outscoring opponents by nearly 40 points per game.

For Sam, it's the second gut-punch blowout in as many weeks: this 71.72-point loss is now the second-worst beating of his four-season career, and paired with last week's 54.96-point loss, two of his three worst-ever defeats have both come in the last two weeks. Sammoth.ai falls to 0-3, and the roster overhaul question is no longer hypothetical.

By the Numbers

Records and Notes From Week 3

Three personal blowout records fell this week. Carston Christensen's 71.72-point win over Sam Trusty is now the third-biggest blowout of his career. Tyson Garff's 56.42-point win over Gavin Chowen cracks his personal top-5. And Sam Trusty's loss lands on his own list too — his second appearance on his personal worst-blowouts list in as many weeks.

Bench management, continued: Britton Anderson left 90.6 points on his bench this week (now his 3rd-highest ever), and Brandon Evans left 72.84 (his 5th-highest, even in a winning effort). Neither approaches Jeffrey Taylor's all-time league record of 118.4 from Week 1, but it's a reminder that even the teams at the top are leaving real points on the table.

Best individual performance: Jahmyr Gibbs, 41.4 points for Auto — his third straight 20+ point week, and real-life analysts are now calling his start one of the best three-game openings by any running back in NFL history.

Standings: Four teams remain unbeaten — Ascension, Cooper Kupping my balls, Shire King, and Team Garff — while three teams (Team Larson, Sammoth.ai, Team Chowen) are still searching for their first win.

Week 4

Division Week Predictions

The schedule flips to Division Week — every game is against a division-mate — and it's delivering the matchup the whole league has been waiting for.

★ Matchup of the Week
Rollin Rockett 🏆
@
Tyson Garff
PICK: Rollin Rockett

The last two undefeated teams left in the league, and they're division rivals. Bijan Robinson has been one of the best fantasy assets in the sport through three weeks, and Rollin's receiving corps (Chris Olave, George Kittle, a resurgent Davante Adams on the roster too) gives him more paths to a big score than Tyson's Josh Allen-and-hope-the-rest-shows-up build. Slight edge to Cooper Kupping my balls in what should be the game of the week.

Britton Anderson
@
Chase Potter 🏆
PICK: Chase Potter

Both teams are 1-2 and looking to build on last week. Ashton Jeanty has been quiet the last two weeks after his monster Week 1, and this is a good bounce-back spot against a Dojah defense-adjacent matchup. Chase Potter at home.

Kaden Smith 🏆
@
Gavin Chowen
PICK: Kaden Smith

Brock Bowers is back and immediately looked like a top-three tight end again, and Ja'Marr Chase has been steady all season. Gavin's De'Von Achane situation shows no signs of turning around, and Team Chowen is 0-3 with real questions about the whole roster construction, not just one player.

Sam Trusty
@
Garrett Larson 🏆
PICK: Garrett Larson

A battle between two 0-3 teams, and someone's misery finally ends. Garrett's new-look receiving corps (Rashee Rice, Davante Adams) both topped 20 points last week, a real sign of life. Sam is coming off back-to-back brutal blowout losses and needs a full-team bounce-back, not just a Justin Jefferson explosion, to snap the skid.

Carston Christensen 🏆
@
Jeffrey Taylor
PICK: Carston Christensen

Ascension is playing at a historic level right now — Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 104 points through three weeks is top-five all-time. Jeffrey is riding a two-game win streak of his own and has the league's best floor at quarterback with Brock Purdy, but this is a tough ask against the best team in the league.

Brandon Evans 🏆
@
Oliver Iverson
PICK: Brandon Evans

Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry remain the best running back duo in the league, and Brandon is 3-0 with the closest game of Week 3 still fresh. Oliver's Jahmyr Gibbs is playing like a top-two running back in the league right now, which keeps this competitive, but the overall roster depth favors Shire King.

Implications

What Week 3 Actually Changed

Ascension isn't just the best team in this league — the numbers say it might be one of the best three-week starts anyone's ever had, in real fantasy football or this one. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's pace is genuinely historic, and Carston Christensen's roster is delivering exactly what the A+ draft grade promised back in Week 1.

On the other end, Sam Trusty's season is unraveling fast. Two of his three worst losses in four years of this league have both come in the last two weeks, and the Justin Jefferson bounce-back bet that anchored his whole draft strategy hasn't materialized — he's averaging under 9 points a game from a receiver who was a top-five pick. Something has to change before this turns into a lost season.

And keep an eye on the Puka Nacua situation for Rollin Rockett: a healthy scratch in his first game with his new team is not the start anyone in that blockbuster trade was hoping for. If he's not producing soon, that trade needs a real second look.

newsletters.title: The Gentlemen's Gazette — Season 4, No. 6 (Week 4 Recap)
newsletters.body:
Week 4 in the Books

A New Blowout King, and Three Teams Still Perfect

Division Week delivered the biggest single-game story of the season: Sam Trusty's 102.22-point demolition of Garrett Larson, now the second-largest margin of victory in four seasons of league history. Meanwhile, the Matchup of the Week lived up to the billing — Rollin Rockett ended Tyson Garff's unbeaten run to keep himself, Carston Christensen, and Brandon Evans alone at the top of the standings at 4-0. Full recap, the new record, and a loaded Week 5 slate below.

SEASON PREDICTION RECORD: 19-5 (79%)
Week 4 Recap

Division Week Results

Britton Anderson 86.74
final
Chase Potter 150.98

CeeDee Lamb (41.3) and Kyren Williams (36.7) combined for nearly 80 points as Chase Potter snapped a two-game slide to move to 2-2. Britton's best moment came from an unlikely source — kicker Will Reichard popped a 19-point outlier — but Dojah falls to 1-3. Predicted: Chase Potter ✅

Kaden Smith 107
final
Gavin Chowen 118.16

Gavin Chowen's first win of the season was a genuine team effort — Alvin Kamara (22.8), Bryce Young (21.46), and Chase Brown (19.1) all chipped in — enough to hold off a huge Javonte Williams game (31.3) for Kaden Smith, who falls to 1-3 despite the fireworks. Predicted: Kaden Smith ❌

Sam Trusty 167.76
final
Garrett Larson 65.54

Tetairoa McMillan exploded for 45.2 points as Sam Trusty put up a season-high 167.76 and blew out Garrett Larson by 102.22 — the second-biggest margin of victory in four seasons of league history, and by a wide margin the biggest win of Sam's own career. Garrett falls to 0-4, with DK Metcalf's 16.5 the lone bright spot. Predicted: Garrett Larson ❌

Rollin Rockett 156.58
final
Tyson Garff 83.22

The Matchup of the Week — full recap below.

Carston Christensen 117.52
final
Jeffrey Taylor 114.92

Two unbeatens-in-spirit traded haymakers. Malik Nabers (23.2) and Quinshon Judkins (21.6) got Carston to 4-0, but Kenneth Walker III's monster 30.9 kept Jeffrey in it until the final whistle — a 2.6-point margin, one of the closest games of Carston's career. Predicted: Carston Christensen ✅

Brandon Evans 126.4
final
Oliver Iverson 121.38

Zay Flowers (25.8) and Jonathan Taylor (22.7) got Brandon to 4-0, but Oliver Iverson's Nico Collins (30.8) and Tee Higgins (26.7) made it a nail-biter — just a 5.02-point margin, the kind of game Shire King has been winning all season. Predicted: Brandon Evans ✅

★ Matchup of the Week Recap
🏈

Cooper Kupping My Balls Stays Perfect, Ends Tyson's Unbeaten Run

Rollin Rockett beat Tyson Garff 156.58–83.22 in a matchup of the league's last two undefeated teams and division rivals. Bijan Robinson (27.7) and a newly-awake Puka Nacua (27.7, his best game yet after last week's healthy scratch) led the way, pushing Rollin to a league-best 4-0 and a league-best +165.1 scoring differential through four weeks.

Tyson's Josh Allen (18.52) and Christian McCaffrey (16.0) simply couldn't keep pace. Team Garff falls to 3-1 — still a clear playoff-caliber roster — but the "two unbeatens colliding" storyline in Division II is over, and Rollin Rockett stands alone as the last team with a perfect record against his own division.

By the Numbers

Records and Notes From Week 4

A new all-time blowout record (almost). Sam Trusty's 102.22-point win over Garrett Larson is now the second-biggest margin of victory in four seasons of league history, trailing only Chase Potter's legendary 146.46-point 2024 playoff blowout. It's also, by a wide margin, the single biggest win of Sam's own four-year career — a stunning turnaround just two weeks removed from back-to-back blowout losses of his own.

A personal record too. Rollin Rockett's 73.36-point win over Tyson Garff is the biggest margin of victory of his own career, cracking his personal top-5 blowouts at #1.

Bench management, continued: Gavin Chowen left 87.02 points on his bench (now his 3rd-highest ever, in a winning effort no less), Carston Christensen left 86.82 (also his 3rd-highest, in a win), and Brandon Evans left 76.36 (his 4th-highest). None approaches Jeffrey Taylor's all-time league record of 118.4 from Week 1, but three of the league's best teams are still leaving real points on the table.

Best individual performance: Tetairoa McMillan, 45.2 points for Sammoth.ai — the headline act in the record-breaking blowout.

Standings: Three teams remain unbeaten after four weeks — Rollin Rockett, Carston Christensen, and Brandon Evans (all 4-0) — after Rollin eliminated the fourth, Tyson Garff, in the Matchup of the Week. Garrett Larson remains winless at 0-4.

Implications

What Week 4 Actually Changed

Sam Trusty's historic blowout doesn't erase an 0-3 start, but it's the kind of result that can flip a season's trajectory — Tetairoa McMillan looked like a true WR1 for the first time all year, and Sam gets Justin Jefferson back in Week 5 to pair with him. 1-3 with real momentum is a very different conversation than 0-4.

At the top, the race for Division II (and the #1 overall seed) just got a lot clearer. Rollin Rockett's win over Tyson Garff wasn't just a Matchup of the Week result — it's a 165.1 scoring differential through four games, the best mark in the league, and a real statement that Cooper Kupping My Balls is the team to beat.

And keep an eye on the bye-week quarterback math in Week 5: Brandon Evans and Gavin Chowen both have to navigate the week without their starting QB, in a game that could otherwise have been a trap for the league's last winless-adjacent team trying to build momentum.
